---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Comprehensive Investment Reserve
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(che, ADD(TS_SUM(capx, 3), invt)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap cash-generative firms with liquidity sufficient relative to both sustained fixed investment and inventory commitments earn higher returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The successful multi-year capex-reserve signal ignores cash tied up in working capital, potentially overstating flexibility for inventory-intensive firms. Adding current inventory creates a broader committed-capital reserve while retaining a bounded, scale-stable construction.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Scalable Capex Reserve
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(che, TS_SUM(capx, 3)))), IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(sale, emp), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap cash-generative firms outperform when multi-year investment reserves coexist with persistent workforce-productivity improvement.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Capex reserves may otherwise identify firms that retain cash by foregoing productive organizational investment. The labor-productivity trend verifies that financial flexibility accompanies scalable operations rather than passive conservatism.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Tangible Post-Investment Optionality
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(che, capx), ADD(ABS(SUB(che, capx)), ppent))), IND_RANK(RATIO(ppent, ADD(ppent, gdwl)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap cash-generative firms that retain liquidity after capex while maintaining tangible operating backing outperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Residual liquidity after investment can favor firms with little installed capital, while a high tangible-to-goodwill share alone can favor capital-heavy firms. Requiring both counterbalances those mechanical tilts and identifies financially flexible firms backed by productive rather than acquisition-premium assets.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Productive Tangible Backing
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(ppent, ADD(ppent, gdwl))), IND_RANK(RATIO(sale, ppent))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap cash-generative firms outperform when tangible capital dominates goodwill and is used intensively to generate sales.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The strong tangible-over-goodwill signal may otherwise select firms merely because they hold large amounts of PP&E. Fixed-asset turnover supplies an opposing PP&E comparative static, requiring tangible backing to be operationally productive rather than simply abundant.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Reserve-Validated Investment Payback
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(che, TS_SUM(capx, 3)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(ebitda, 1), ADD(ABS(DELTA(ebitda, 1)), LAG(capx, 1))))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap cash-generative firms with both adequate multi-year investment reserves and strong operating-profit payback earn higher returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Reserve strength alone can reflect underinvestment, while one-period payback can be fragile when firms lack capacity to sustain future projects. The interaction requires demonstrated investment productivity alongside financial ability to continue investing.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Organization-Validated Investment Payback
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(ebitda, 1), ADD(ABS(DELTA(ebitda, 1)), LAG(capx, 1)))), IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(sale, emp), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap cash-generative firms outperform when capital expenditure generates operating-profit growth alongside persistent workforce-productivity improvement.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: EBITDA payback can arise from temporary cost reductions rather than durable investment success. Requiring a sustained rise in sales per employee validates that the payoff is supported by broader organizational scalability.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Capex-Volatility Reserve Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(che, VOL(capx, 3)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap cash-generative firms with cash reserves sufficient to absorb uncertainty in capital spending earn higher returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: This replaces the cumulative-capex denominator with the dollar volatility of the investment program, introducing a funding-uncertainty comparative static rather than another reserve-horizon variant. Cash and capex volatility are both dollar stocks of available resources versus investment risk, so the bounded ratio measures shock capacity directly.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Workforce-Productivity Resilience Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_MIN(RATIO(sale, emp), 5), TS_MAX(RATIO(sale, emp), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap firms that preserve sales per employee through their operating cycle earn higher subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: The minimum-to-maximum ratio measures the downside resilience of labor productivity rather than its trend or its interaction with a liquidity proxy. Normalizing by each firm’s own productivity peak also avoids rewarding firms solely for operating at a structurally high sales-per-employee level.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Persistent Reinvestment Efficiency Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), IND_RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(SUB(DELTA(ebitda, 1), DELTA(capx, 1)), 0), 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap cash-generative firms that repeatedly grow operating profit faster than capital spending earn higher returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This replaces the one-period optionality-payback intersection with a persistence count of periods in which incremental EBITDA exceeds incremental capex. The count is insensitive to the magnitude of isolated accounting outliers and tests whether disciplined reinvestment efficiency recurs rather than appearing once.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Stable-Workforce Margin Expansion
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(RATIO(ebitda, sale), 1), ADD(ABS(DELTA(RATIO(ebitda, sale), 1)), ABS(GROWTH(emp, 1))))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap cash-generative firms whose operating margins expand without large headcount changes earn higher subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: This directly compares margin improvement with the magnitude of labor investment adjustment instead of stacking capex payback and workforce-productivity gates. Penalizing both aggressive hiring and large layoffs helps isolate scalable process improvement rather than expansion-driven or retrenchment-driven margin changes.
